title: Establishment of Dittrichia viscosa L. hairy roots and improvement of bioactive compound production
why: Dittrichia sense_chemical: the web search "Dittrichia viscosa methyl jasmonate elicitation" (run after "Dittrichia response to volatiles methyl jasmonate ethylene" returned untitled records of the Instituto Politecnico de Braganca repository, bibliotecadigital.ipb.pt handle 10198/13548 and publication f023f7fe-0e0e-4f52-80b2-081b05f0effe, in both searches) returned this title, which suggests D. viscosa hairy roots treated with elicitors such as methyl jasmonate; audit 78 found main logging elicitor and hormone responses of living plants under sense_chemical. The listing gave no authors, year or DOI, and nothing was opened; the IPB records may be the same work. One fork stays open for the owner: a hairy-root culture is transformed tissue grown apart from the plant, which reading 10(a) may treat as tissue taken from the plant.

title: Long-day perennials
why: Sidalcea sense_light_nonvisual: the follow-up web search "Sidalcea long day short day flowering photoperiod perennials" (after "Sidalcea light response photoperiod" and "checkerbloom light response photoperiod", which returned only general photoperiodism pages, Gene Ontology terms and an untitled natuurtijdschriften.nl record, pub/539144) returned this Michigan State University extension sheet and its PDF first, with a vernalization sheet from the same series (canr.msu.edu/uploads/resources/pdfs/vernalizationpart4.pdf). Such sheets list perennials whose flowering the university's greenhouse trials found promoted by long days; if Sidalcea is listed, its flowering response to day length is a light response of the kind main logs for Mentha piperita (sweep-100:1). The page was not opened; no author, year or DOI was shown.

title: The impact of photoperiod and irradiance on flowering of several herbaceous ornamentals
why: Antennaria sense_light_nonvisual: the web search "Antennaria light response photoperiod" returned this University of Minnesota experts page (title cut short in the listing as "the impact of photoperiod and irradiance on flowering of several"), a study of how day length and irradiance change flowering in a set of herbaceous ornamentals; if an Antennaria is among the species, its flowering response is a light response of the kind main logs for Mentha piperita (sweep-100:1). title: Night-time control of carbohydrate availability in grasses differs radically from that in Arabidopsis
why: Lagurus diel: the harvest query "Lagurus photoperiod" (run 3, supplement run 14) returned this preprint, whose abstract reports day accumulation and night-time depletion of sucrose and starch in leaf blades of 41 species of pooid grasses; Lagurus ovatus is a pooid grass, and the harvest match suggests the text names it. A day and night carbohydrate turnover measured in a Lagurus would be a daily rhythm of the living plant. One fork stays open for the owner: the desk's plant diel words are flower opening times, and audit 77 left open whether a daily physiological rhythm closes a plant's diel cell. The web searches "Lagurus flower opening time anthesis", "hare's-tail grass flower opening time anthesis" and "10.3389/fpls.2018.01585" returned no Lagurus anthesis-hour study (species pages, the anthesis Wikipedia page, a Darwin manuscript transcription, CUL DAR49.44, and a Frontiers 2018 article whose subject stayed unread). Not opened.

title: Light environment and epidermal cell morphology in grasses
why: Lagurus sense_light_nonvisual: the web search "hare's-tail grass plant ocelli lens-like epidermal cells eye" returned this University of Washington publication page (Stromberg laboratory) under three addresses. A grass study relating leaf epidermal cell shape to the light environment may include Lagurus ovatus; if it reports a within-species change of epidermal cells with shade or open light, that is a light response main could log for the genus, while a comparison between species in different habitats would not be. The searches "Lagurus light response photoperiod" and "hare's-tail grass light response photoperiod" returned general photoperiod pages, a Benary seed page for Lagurus ovatus Bunny, a Planta article page (10.1007/BF00387918, subject not shown), a JIRCAS JARQ PDF (22-4, pages 247-252, subject not shown) and Setaria and Bouteloua photoperiod papers, none naming Lagurus in the title. The page was not opened; no authors, year or DOI were shown.

Genista sense_chemical: the follow-up web search "Genista tinctoria elicitor isoflavones jasmonic acid treatment" (after "Genista volatile emission jasmonate ethylene response" and "French broom volatile emission jasmonate ethylene response" returned only general induced-volatile works on other plants and a potato study exposed to French marigold essential oil) returned this Springer article page without a readable title, beside works on isoflavone production by Genista tinctoria in vitro cultures: a suspension culture treated with vanadium compounds (PMC6099964, Molecules 2018), which reading 10(a) excludes as tissue taken from the plant, and a Charles University thesis titled Genista tinctoria L. in vitro, on influencing secondary metabolite production. If this article reports an elicitor or hormone response of rooted plants or shoot cultures, it is the kind of row main logs under sense_chemical (audit 78); one fork stays open for the owner, whether an in vitro shoot culture counts as tissue taken from the plant. Not opened; title, authors and year were not shown.
